newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cold winter last year boosts German '96 energy use.
newsitem.headline: Cold winter last year boosts German '96 energy use.

text.p: The cold weather Germany experienced twelve months ago gave consumption of heating oil and natural gas a boost in 1996, Exxon Corp unit Esso AG said on Thursday.

With average temperatures around 15 percent lower compared to the previous year, primary energy sales grew nearly three percent to 500 million tonnes of hard coal units in 1996, while petroleum consumption grew marginally, up 1.4 percent to 128 million tonnes.
Cold weather at the start of 1996 lifted demand for domestic heating oil by 10 percent, Esso said. Natural gas registered the biggest increase of all energy types, up 12 percent.
However, demand for petrol and diesel for cars remained in 1996 around the previous year's level, even though the number of cars sold grew by 1.8 percent.
Esso said that sinking incomes meant that people were not travelling as much and that the consumption of petrol in new cars was lower.
